posts.title: Weekly update 2: Assault, King of the Hill and Saturday's playtest
posts.author: MJOLNIR Core
posts.summary: Assault, King, Oddball and Race reach the maps, a marker points you to the objective, and Yoyorast Island gets the Mongoose. Most of it has only run on our own test PCs, so join Saturday's playtest and help us find what breaks.
posts.body:
Weekly updates now come out on Saturdays, the day of our playtest, so each one can tell you what's new and what we most need tested that evening.

This was a big week. Assault completes Halo CE's Standard game types, and 46 maps were updated to offer them. Until today nearly all of it had only run on one PC. We ran it between two of our PCs today and fixed what turned up, so this Saturday matters more than most.

## Saturday's playtest

- **When:** [Saturday, November 7, 6 PM MST](https://discord.gg/AQnRCHbmXq?event=1556902193548886056 "2026-11-08T01:00:00Z")
- **Join us:** the [Discord event](https://discord.gg/AQnRCHbmXq?event=1556902193548886056). Click Interested and Discord will tell you when it starts.
- **Watch:** [twitch.tv/devnull9090](https://www.twitch.tv/devnull9090)

We play every Saturday at this time, so if you can't make this one, come to the next.

### Before you join

1. **Open the [launcher](/download) early and let it update.** It brings your mods to 0.46.4 and your maps up to date. This week's map updates come to about 1.5 GB if you have every map.
2. **Install [Yoyorast Island](/mods/ce-yoyorast-island-v2) and check it says 2.7.1.** Earlier versions don't have the map's gates and buttons.

### What to test

We'll start on Yoyorast Island and work down the list. All of this needs real players, because bots can't hold a hill, carry a ball or take over as the Juggernaut.

1. **Joining.** Everyone loads in and sees the same score. Everyone sees the two Mongooses at the top of the ramp, and a joiner hears a vehicle's engine and sees it move. If the host picks a map you don't have, you should be told which map and offered its download.
2. **Gates, shields and teleporters.** Nobody has used these with a second player yet. Press a button as a joiner. Does the gate rise for everyone, block players and vehicles, and drop after 60 seconds? Does a panic shield come up, block, and drop after a minute? If someone joins while a gate is up, do they see it up? Do the teleporters work both ways?
3. **The Mongoose.** Drive it off a high ledge onto the beach, where it should land on its wheels and drive away. Brake hard with someone watching from behind: the lamps should glow. Carry a second player on the back, and check you both see the same thing.
4. **Assault.** It has never been played by two people. One flag starts on Blue's stand. Red can take it and Blue can't. A capture moves the flag to Red's stand with Blue attacking. Five minutes with no capture sends the flag home and swaps the sides. Three captures win. Check that the flag's marker stays on it for everyone, that only one flag shows after a capture, and that ATTACK or DEFEND is right on each player's screen.
5. **Capture the Flag and Team Slayer.** You can only score while your own flag is home. A dropped flag goes back when its own team touches it. Every Warthog and Mongoose should be on the map. With three or more players, killing a teammate costs a point.
6. **King of the Hill.** A second player on the hill stops the scoring, and every screen should say HILL CONTESTED. In Crazy King the hill moves every minute, so tell us if it ever lands somewhere you can't reach. In Team King, teammates shouldn't contest each other.
7. **Oddball, Juggernaut, Stalker and Reverse Tag.** Killing the carrier drops the ball. Killing the Juggernaut, the Stalker or whoever is "it" should pass the role to you, on every player's screen.
8. **Race and Rally.** Nobody has driven a lap yet. Yoyorast's is 27 flags and about 2.2 km. Take a Warthog or Mongoose round and tell us about any flag you can't reach. In Rally, touching the live flag should score and move it somewhere else.
9. **Forge.** Host Forge. The map's vehicles should be there, and a joiner should see them too. Grab one with the Monitor, move it, press F5, then host Slayer: it should start at its new spot.
10. **Leaving.** When the host picks SAVE AND EXIT, the host should go back to the lobby with no vote. A match that ends on its own should still hold a vote, and everyone should travel to the winner.

If something breaks, note which item it was. Before you close the game, copy `Meteorite\Binaries\Win64\ue4ss\UE4SS.log` from your game folder and post it in our [Discord](https://discord.gg/9gxYZsByW9). The full checklist is [on GitHub](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/docs/playtest_yoyorast.md).

## Assault

One flag at a time. The attackers carry it to their own base while the defenders stop them, and a capture or five minutes on the clock swaps the sides. Three captures win. It's under Capture the Flag on every map that has CTF.

![Assault on Blood Gulch: attacking Blue's base, with the flag 51 metres away and the sides swapping in 2:10.](/blog-images/weekly-update-2/assault-blood-gulch.jpg)

A line under the score says whether you're attacking or defending, and counts down to the next swap. If you join a game already running, the countdown starts at the first swap you see.

## King, Oddball and Race on 46 maps

Game types only appear on a map that carries their hills, balls and flags, so we rebuilt 46 of the 51 maps to carry them:

- **The nineteen classic maps and Yoyorast Island** have King, Oddball and Race.
- **Coldsnap and all 25 Halo 2 maps** have King and Oddball.

Each of those comes in variants: King, Crazy King and Team King; Oddball and Team Oddball; Race, Team Race, Rally and Team Rally. Three more game types are on every map with Slayer:

- **Juggernaut:** the first kill makes you the Juggernaut, and killing the Juggernaut takes over. It deals half as much damage again as everyone else, melee included.
- **Stalker:** the first kill makes you the Stalker, invisible and fast, while everyone else takes half damage. Kill the Stalker to take over.
- **Reverse Tag:** the first kill makes you it. Whoever is it moves slowly and scores a point a second until someone kills them.

That makes 17 game types on Blood Gulch alone. The same map updates also stop you respawning on a health pack's spot on the Halo CE maps.

The hill stands out from across the map. A wall of plasma rings it and a beacon rises from it, gold when it's empty, cyan when you hold it, orange-red when someone else does, and flashing violet when it's contested. One rule to know: unlike Halo CE, a contested hill scores for nobody, as in Reach. This look reached players today with CE runtime 1.19.0, which the launcher installs.

![An empty hill on Blood Gulch: a gold wall of plasma around the hill, with a beacon rising from the middle.](/blog-images/weekly-update-2/king-hill.jpg)

![The same hill held by the player: the wall and beacon turn cyan, ON THE HILL shows under the score, and the score climbs.](/blog-images/weekly-update-2/king-on-the-hill.jpg)

## A marker that shows you the way

A badge now sits over the hill, the next Race flag or the Juggernaut, with the distance under it. Capture the Flag and Assault show one for each flag, in its team's colour, and it stays on the flag when it's dropped or carried.

![The hill's marker on Blood Gulch, 20 metres away and below the player, in front of its beacon.](/blog-images/weekly-update-2/marker-beacon.jpg)

When the spot is out of view, the badge slides to the edge of the screen and points the way to turn. It pulses when a hill is contested, and fades when it's over your crosshair so you can still aim. The Stalker never gets one.

![With the hill behind the player, the marker sits at the left edge of the screen and points the way to turn, 92 metres out.](/blog-images/weekly-update-2/marker-edge.jpg)

The line under the score now says only what the marker can't, such as ON THE HILL, HILL CONTESTED or LAP 1 OF 3.

## New game type and map screens

With this many game types, the old tiles couldn't cope. The game type screen now shows seven families, each naming its variants, and the family you pick lists them as buttons on the right. SELECT says exactly what you chose.

![The game type screen: seven families on the left, with Capture the Flag open and its Assault variant chosen on the right.](/blog-images/weekly-update-2/game-type-screen.jpg)

Map select uses the same families as tabs, and the tab you pick opens a tray with its description and variants.

![Map select's game type tabs, with Juggernaut open and its three variants below.](/blog-images/weekly-update-2/map-select-tabs.jpg)

## The Mongoose and Yoyorast Island

[Yoyorast Island](/mods/ce-yoyorast-island-v2) is the first Custom Edition map to bring its own vehicle. The Mongoose has its own engine sounds, headlights and tail lamps, and carries a driver and a passenger. Version 2.7.1 also brings the map's buttons, gates and panic shields, and it offers every game type on the list above.

![A Mongoose on Yoyorast Island, with a Spartan ahead of it and the island's tower beyond.](/blog-images/weekly-update-2/mongoose-yoyorast.jpg)

Its handling isn't final, and it still shows the Warthog's HUD icons. Tell us how it drives.

## Forge

- **A converted map's vehicles now appear in Forge.** Before, Forge showed none of them on a converted Custom Edition map. It now starts with the ones a Slayer game would place, and they stay when you load a saved layout.
- **F2 can't quietly lose your save.** One press used to move your saved layout into history with nothing on screen. It now takes two presses, and the first tells you what will happen.
- **F6 brings a reverted save back,** even after a restart. Objects you placed after your last save are still lost by a revert.

## Fixed today

We played this week's game types between two of our PCs today, one hosting and one joining, and fixed what we found. Two of these fixes help when you play alone too.

- **Everyone is where they really are.** On a joiner's screen, the marker on the Juggernaut, or on whoever was it in Reverse Tag, pointed at the middle of the map. The scoreboard didn't know the teams either, so a joiner had no "/ YOU" and no ATTACK or DEFEND line. Markers now follow the player, and every team shows from the start.
- **HILL CONTESTED shows.** With two players on the hill, both screens said ON THE HILL while nobody scored. Now they say HILL CONTESTED, and a hill someone else holds shows in their colour.
- **One flag in Assault.** After a capture, a joiner could keep a ghost of the old flag, with a second marker and a swap clock stuck at 0:00.
- **Quitting goes to the lobby.** A host who picked SAVE AND EXIT could land on the post-game vote, and the next match started 20 seconds later. A match that ends on its own still votes.
- **The vote offers only maps you have installed.** If a chosen game can't start, everyone goes back to the lobby and is told why.
- **Missing a map? You're told which one.** A joiner without the host's map, or with another version of it, saw only CONNECTION LOST. Now you see which map it was and its download screen. DOWNLOAD installs it without a restart, then you can join again. A kick shows the host's reason, and the screen stays up until you've read it.
- **The right number of Spartan bots.** When bots started before anyone had spawned, as in Forge, eight bots could become thirty-two, none of them on the board.
- **Yoyorast's sea.** The island could load with bare sand where the sea should be. The loader now notices and fixes it as the map loads.

They're in [mods 0.46.1](/changelog/mods/0.46.1) to [0.46.4](/changelog/mods/0.46.4).

## Player pages and leaderboards

Every player's page now has a combat record: a career ring with a spoke for each match, form over time, where they killed and died on each map, their arsenal, rivals and medals.

![A combat record: career kills per death on the left, and a ring on the right with a spoke for each match, kills reaching out and deaths reaching in.](/blog-images/weekly-update-2/combat-record.jpg)

The new [leaderboards](/leaderboards) rank Kills, K/D, Wins, Win rate, Headshots and Best match, over all time, 30 days or 7 days. To place, link your account from the game. A match counts when at least two linked accounts played in it, so a board can read lower than a career total.

## A smoother launcher

- **Launching works again.** After mods 0.44.0, some launches stopped with Try again, and trying again failed the same way. Launcher 0.22.0 fixes that, updates itself, and finishes the update it couldn't complete.
- **A refused mod is left as it was.** The launcher now checks every file in a mod before it writes any of them, so a bad file can't leave a mod half-installed.
- **Update checks are quicker** on a long map list.

## For modders and map makers

- **Custom vehicles, scripts and devices.** [CLI 0.8.0](/changelog/cli/0.8.0) carries a Custom Edition map's own vehicles, scripts, buttons, gates and automatic doors into a level, and writes King, Oddball, Race and their variants. See [custom vehicles](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/docs/custom_vehicles.md) and [CE map conversion](/docs/notes/ce-map-conversion).
- **Animation graphs.** [CLI 0.9.0](/changelog/cli/0.9.0) adds `mjolnir jmad`, which reads a graph, rewrites it for another skeleton, and proves a round trip byte for byte. The format is [documented](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/docs/jmad_format.md).
- **Package tools.** `mjolnir ue scan` searches the game's packages and `mjolnir ue clone` copies one under your own path. Nobody has loaded a cloned package in the game yet.
- **Game types with traits.** `mjolnir megalo write` now writes game types that change a player's traits, including Stalker and Reverse Tag.
- **Vehicle sound banks.** [Launcher 0.23.0](/changelog/launcher/0.23.0) and [CLI 0.10.0](/changelog/cli/0.10.0) let a map carry Wwise banks for its own vehicles, so they follow your volume sliders. No published map uses them yet, so nothing changes today.
- **Clearer reviews.** Authors now see every release they've uploaded, and the moderator's reason for any held back.

## Versions

| Product | Now at | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Launcher | [0.23.0](/changelog/launcher/0.23.0) | From 0.21.0 |
| Code mods | [0.46.4](/changelog/mods/0.46.4) | From 0.43.1 |
| CE runtime | 1.19.0 | The launcher installs it |
| CLI | [0.10.0](/changelog/cli/0.10.0) | From 0.7.0. Scoop and Homebrew are still on 0.9.0 |
| Tag editor | [0.25.0](/changelog/tag-editor/0.25.0) | No change this week |

Every release is listed in the [changelog](/changelog).

## See you Saturday

Update the [launcher](/download) before 6 PM, [join the event](https://discord.gg/AQnRCHbmXq?event=1556902193548886056), and come break things with us. If you can't play, [watch on Twitch](https://www.twitch.tv/devnull9090) and tell us what you spot in our [Discord](https://discord.gg/9gxYZsByW9).

posts.title: How 25 Halo 2 maps came to Campaign Evolved
posts.author: MJOLNIR Core
posts.summary: Lockout first loaded with a black sky and rooms too dark to see. Three days later, all 25 Halo 2 maps were on the Hub, and today their lifts went live. Here's what it took: a new file format, unlabelled shaders, moving collision and many white rectangles.
posts.body:
![Lockout, from the first boot to the sky it has now](/blog-images/halo-2-maps/lockout-clouds.jpg?before=/blog-images/halo-2-maps/lockout-first-boot.jpg&labels=First%20boot,Now)

That's Lockout on the first day it loaded in Halo Campaign Evolved, and the same view from a few builds later. Drag the divider to compare.

Halo Campaign Evolved is a Halo 1 game. Its simulation has never heard of Halo 2, yet you can now host Lockout, Zanzibar, Ascension and 22 other Halo 2 maps from the multiplayer menu, with [bots](/blog/weekly-update-1), Slayer and CTF. Lockout first played on October 21, all 25 maps reached [the Hub](/maps) on October 24, and their lifts arrived today.

We already had a way to bring [classic Halo CE maps](/blog/lighting-the-classics) into the game. This is the story of what changed when the maps came from a different game.

## Teaching the tools a second game

Our converter starts from Halo 2's maps in The Master Chief Collection, and those files look nothing like Halo CE's. They are compressed in chunks. Every texture's pixels sit in a separate `textures.dat`, every sound in separate `.dat` files, and every weapon, vehicle and most shaders in a `shared.map` that all the maps lean on.

So `mjolnir cache` learned to read the file header, name the game a map came from and unpack Halo 2's data into the same files we produce for a Halo 1 map, in the same units and axes. Everything after that step works on either game's maps.

That left one rule: Halo 2 could not break Halo 1. We reconverted Chill Out from start to finish with the new code, and it came out byte for byte identical to the released map.

## First boot: a sky 3 metres wide

Two of the first bugs are in that picture at the top.

**The black sky.** Halo 2 squeezes a model's positions into a range of -1 to 1 across its bounding box. We read those numbers as they were, so Lockout's whole sky became a 3 metre knot at the centre of the world.

**The dark rooms.** Halo 2 stores its lightmaps at half brightness and doubles them in the shader. Our materials take a lightmap as it comes, so we now double them during conversion.

With those fixed, Lockout had a sky of sorts, and a new problem.

![Lockout's sky as flat white planes, then as the cloud banks and mountains it should be](/blog-images/halo-2-maps/lockout-clouds.jpg?before=/blog-images/halo-2-maps/lockout-white-planes.jpg&labels=White%20planes,Cloud%20banks)

## Shaders with the labels removed

Those white planes are clouds. Most of the work on these maps went into problems like this one.

Halo CE's shaders are a short list of types with named fields. Halo 2 has a large set of shader templates, and the MCC files no longer keep the names of their inputs. A shader says "use these bitmaps with these numbers" without saying what any of them mean.

The answer is in the map files, though, because the compiled shaders are in there too. We read them back one template at a time and rebuilt the maths in our own materials. A cloud bank turned out to be a mask times two scrolling layers. The fog-like gas in Lockout's chambers is the same recipe.

![Green gas drifting behind the glass of Lockout's chambers.](/blog-images/halo-2-maps/lockout-chamber-gas.jpg)

To find what was left, we toured all the maps and listed every template with no code of its own. Whatever the converter didn't recognise had been drawn as a plain opaque surface, or from one bitmap alone, and the results were easy to spot:

- **Desolation's light shafts** were solid white slabs until they faded by viewing angle, as Halo 2's do.
- **Covenant holo panels** on Midship, Desolation and Gemini were white blocks.
- **Beaver Creek's creek** was a glossy, unmoving picture. It now uses Halo CE's water, with moving ripples.
- **Zanzibar's beach** had a big white patch, which was a plane Halo 2 only uses as a mask for its water.
- **Zanzibar's palms** lost their leaf shapes, because those shapes are stored in the bump map's alpha channel and not the base map's.
- **Backwash's sky** drew black above the swamp fog, because Halo 2's fog covers the sky too.

![Beaver Creek from above, its creek running through the canyon.](/blog-images/halo-2-maps/beaver-creek.jpg)

![Backwash's swamp, lost in its heavy green fog.](/blog-images/halo-2-maps/backwash.jpg)

Ascension's sea of cloud fooled us for a while. It looks like fog, but it's a transparent plane of cloud puffs sitting under the fog layer, with a second cloud texture scrolling across it. Once we drew it that way, wisps drifted through it, and we checked the result side by side with MCC.

![Ascension's rocks standing in a flat grey plane, then in a sea of drifting cloud](/blog-images/halo-2-maps/ascension-cloud-sea.jpg?before=/blog-images/halo-2-maps/ascension-flat-sea.jpg&labels=Flat%20plane,Cloud%20sea)

## The world underneath

Looks are only half of a map. The Halo simulation does all the collision, and it never looks at what Unreal draws, so it needs its own copy of every wall and floor.

Halo 2's collision is close to Halo CE's but stored in smaller tables, so we widen it into the older layout. Halo 2 also reuses pieces of level geometry many times, which Halo CE never did, so each copy is placed in the world and added to the collision. On Lockout, that's 3,162 surfaces in the main level, 7,312 triangles from 75 placed pieces and 840 more from 15 crates. Every surface also needs a material, so bullets and footsteps behave. Halo 2's materials map onto the 29 the game ships, closest match first.

The maps needed some game rules translated too. Halo 2 picks spawns by influence, so Lockout's starting points have no team at all. Each one now takes the side of the nearest CTF flag, which gives CTF real red and blue spawns.

Weapons are where you'll notice the translation most. For now, several Halo 2 weapons spawn as stand-ins: the battle rifle as an assault rifle, the brute shot as a fuel rod gun, and the carbine, brute plasma rifle and sentinel beam as plasma rifles.

## Making Ascension's antennas turn

Ascension's great antennas swing around the map every 40 seconds. Turning the art is easy. The collision is the hard part, because the simulation's level collision can't move, so a solid arm would stay where it started while the picture of it swung away.

We tried moving the object directly. The object moved, and its physics stayed behind. The only thing the simulation moves properly is a device machine, the kind of object an elevator is. The campaign has an elevator on *Assault on the Control Room*, so each turning part in Halo 2 became a new machine cloned from that one, with Halo 2's collision and a new animation.

![Ascension's antennas at two moments of their turn](/blog-images/halo-2-maps/ascension-arms-b.jpg?before=/blog-images/halo-2-maps/ascension-arms-a.jpg&labels=One%20moment,Seconds%20later)

Three bugs came with it, each a small puzzle:

- **Falling through.** Our first arms were built from physics boxes, and players dropped straight through them. Players collide with a machine's collision model, not its physics boxes.
- **The wobble.** We set the machine's "transition time" to 40 seconds, and the antennas shook. The engine reads that field as a rate, so they were turning 40 times a second, and it looked like a slow wobble.
- **The pause.** Zanzibar's wheel turned for 24 seconds of every 30, then stopped for 6. The engine counts animation frames differently from Halo 2, so the wheel finished its circle early and waited.

You can now stand on an antenna arm and ride it around. Zanzibar's wheel and flywheels and Foundation's fans work the same way.

![Zanzibar from above, with its great wheel beside the sea wall.](/blog-images/halo-2-maps/zanzibar.jpg)

## Lifts: the code shipped, the data didn't

Halo 2's lifts, jump pads and vents don't exist as Halo CE objects. They are phantoms: invisible shapes that nothing collides with, each with a direction and a push. Nothing in the simulation pushes a player the way these do, so our level loader does the work. It watches for a player inside a phantom and sets their velocity every 50 milliseconds. Each player's own game pushes them, because a push the host sends to a joiner's character does nothing.

This went into the mods on October 25, and it worked: Lockout's lift threw us out onto the top floor. Then we got caught out by our own pipeline. That test used a freshly converted Lockout. The maps on the Hub were converted before lifts existed, and the later releases only added bots to them, so no published map had the lift data. Our changelog said the lift worked, and it did, just not on the map you'd downloaded.

Lift data is only read by the loader, so we didn't need to convert anything again. `add_lifts.py` adds the lifts to each map's level file and refuses to continue if anything else in the map changes. **As of today, 14 maps are at version 1.3.0 with their lifts, so update your maps to get them:** Ascension, Backwash, Coagulation, Colossus, Desolation, Foundation, Gemini, Headlong, Ivory Tower, Lockout, Midship, Relic, Tombstone and Warlock. The other 11 have no player lifts and stay at 1.2.0.

**These are less tested than we'd like, and we'd like your help.** A script flew a test player into 30 of the 54 lifts, pads and vents, across 12 of the 14 maps. Only Lockout's lift has been ridden from the bottom. We haven't yet tried these:

- **Coagulation's and Headlong's lifts and Backwash's main lifts**, which the test didn't reach.
- **A vent from the bottom.** The test entered vent shafts near the top.
- **A joiner riding a lift** in a real match between two PCs.
- **Speeds and heights against Halo 2.** Ascension's jump pad reached about 32 m/s, and we don't know yet how that compares.

If a lift throws you somewhere odd, please tell us which map and which lift.

## Sound

Halo 2's sounds live in those separate `.dat` files, as Opus audio and Xbox ADPCM, with no headers to say where anything starts. The converter pulls them out and brings them in beside the map, so you get the background loops, the hums of placed objects and, on Ascension, the antennas' own sound cues, timed to their turn.

## What still isn't there

We'd rather you hear these from us:

- **Doors and other sliding parts don't move,** and neither do Terminal's train or Backwash's monitor.
- **Colossus's and Terminal's lightning isn't drawn,** and Tombstone's viewscreen is missing.
- **Random detail sounds,** such as Ascension's thunder and wind gusts, aren't played yet.
- **Bots don't ride lifts,** so on maps like Lockout they stay near where they spawn.
- **Halo 2's own weapons** are stand-ins, as above.

![Relic's island in its dark sea.](/blog-images/halo-2-maps/relic.jpg)

## Read the code

The Halo 2 conversion is in our public repository. If you want the full detail, every shader template included, start with these:

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| The whole conversion, step by step | [`docs/h2_map_conversion.md`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/docs/h2_map_conversion.md) |
| Halo 2's file format | [`docs/h2_cache_format.md`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/docs/h2_cache_format.md) |
| What was tested for the lift release | [`docs/h2_lifts_release.md`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/docs/h2_lifts_release.md) |
| Turning parts into machines | [`tools/level/h2_machines.py`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/tools/level/h2_machines.py) |
| Adding lifts to published maps | [`tools/level/add_lifts.py`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/tools/level/add_lifts.py) |
| How classic maps are converted | [Halo CE map conversion](/docs/notes/ce-map-conversion) |

All 25 maps are [on the Hub](/maps), or use the Install Halo 2 maps button on the launcher's Multiplayer page. Go and ride something.

posts.title: Weekly update 1: AI bots, Halo 2 maps, Forge and everything since October 17
posts.author: MJOLNIR Core
posts.summary: Our first weekly update catches up on two and a half busy weeks: AI bots, all 25 Halo 2 maps, Forge, Team Slayer, match chat, Discord presence, a smarter launcher, faster map loads and a long list of fixes.
posts.body:
A lot of what we build disappears into changelogs, so starting today we will post an update every week: what changed, what to try, and where to read more.

This first one is a catch-up. Our last general update was [the remastered maps](/blog/ce-maps-remastered) on October 17, and a great deal has landed since. Multiplayer now has bots and 25 more maps, and you can build your own layouts in Forge.

## Try this week

Update the [launcher](/download) first. It installs everything else you need. Then:

1. **Fill a match with bots.** Host any map, open the game settings, and set BOTS on the PLAYERS page.
2. **Install the Halo 2 maps** with the Install Halo 2 maps button on the launcher's Multiplayer page.
3. **Play Team Slayer or CTF** with a few friends, now that team games start properly with three or more players.
4. **Build something in Forge.** Start with [your first Forge build](/docs/guides/forge-guide).
5. **Say hello in match chat.** Press T.

## AI bots in multiplayer

You no longer need a full fireteam to play. The host can add up to 15 bots from the PLAYERS page of the game settings, choosing Spartans, Elites, Grunts, Jackals or a mix, at Normal, Heroic or Legendary. They have names, appear on the scoreboard and in the kill feed, and respawn 5 seconds after they die. Spartan bots wear classic armour and carry a mixed arsenal, including the sniper rifle and rocket launcher where the map has them.

![A Team Slayer scoreboard on Blood Gulch with named bots on the red and blue teams, and the first kill on the board.](/blog-images/weekly-update-1/bots-scoreboard.jpg)

In team games, bots play for red and blue. Each one joins the side with fewer players, leaves its teammates alone, and fights the other side. Their kills count toward the team score, and a player who kills a bot on their own side is charged with a betrayal. Bots also come in near their own side, spread out across the map, and no longer stand still for minutes while taking fire. In Free for All they hunt players but don't fight each other.

The host can change bots mid-match in chat: `/bots 6 elites heroic`.

![A blue Spartan bot crossing the long grass at Blood Gulch.](/blog-images/weekly-update-1/bots-blood-gulch.jpg)

Bots work on all nineteen classic maps, all 25 Halo 2 maps, Yoyorast Island, Coldsnap and Night Lockout. Make sure your maps are up to date, because the BOTS setting does nothing on an older release.

**What bots can't do yet:** they walk, but they don't jump, ride lifts or use teleporters. On maps whose floors are joined only that way, such as Lockout, Boarding Action and Chiron TL-34, they stay near where they spawn. On Gemini they can't cross between the islands. Night Lockout's bots play its lower level only. The new Forge maps don't have bots yet.

Map makers can add bots to their own levels with [CLI 0.7.0](/changelog/cli/0.7.0) and the `blam.bots` section of the [level format](/docs/notes/level-format).

## All 25 Halo 2 multiplayer maps

Ascension, Backwash, Beaver Creek, Burial Mounds, Coagulation, Colossus, Containment, Desolation, District, Elongation, Foundation, Gemini, Headlong, Ivory Tower, Lockout, Midship, Relic, Sanctuary, Terminal, Tombstone, Turf, Uplift, Warlock, Waterworks and Zanzibar are all [on the Hub](/maps).

![Lockout in Halo Campaign Evolved, looking across the gap between the towers.](/blog-images/weekly-update-1/lockout.jpg)

![Zanzibar from above, with its turning wheel, sea wall and beach.](/blog-images/weekly-update-1/h2-zanzibar.jpg)

![Uplift's beach and bridge beneath the canyon, with the beam firing into the sky.](/blog-images/weekly-update-1/h2-uplift.jpg)

![Midship, the Covenant ship, from outside.](/blog-images/weekly-update-1/h2-midship.jpg)

![Containment's snowy valley from above.](/blog-images/weekly-update-1/h2-containment.jpg)

Each one offers Slayer and CTF, and the set is an optional download of about 586 MB. Moving scenery turns as it should, with working collision: Zanzibar's wheel, Ascension's antennas and Foundation's fans.

**New on November 4:** gravity lifts, jump pads and vents now work on the 14 Halo 2 maps that have them, in version 1.3.0 of those maps, so update your maps to get them. They've had less testing than we'd like, so please tell us if one throws you somewhere odd. Doors and other sliding parts don't move yet. The story of how these maps were made is in [How 25 Halo 2 maps came to Campaign Evolved](/blog/halo-2-maps).

Hosts no longer need every map installed first. SELECT MAP lists up to 80 maps, including Hub maps you don't have yet, marked DOWNLOAD. Chips filter by game and source, and a search box finds a map by name, code or game.

## Forge

Forge arrived on October 24 as a way to move a map's objects around. Ten days later, you can place new objects from the map's palette, set their team, label, respawn time and spawn order, and save your work. **F5** saves a layout, **F6** loads it, and **F2** goes back to the map's own. A saved layout starts every game you host on that map, in Slayer and CTF as well as Forge, and players who join see your objects.

![Crossline from above, built from the Foundry Wide kit.](/blog-images/forge-building/crossline-overview.webp)

Modular kits followed on November 3: Foundry, Foundry Wide and Roadworks, along with the Crossline, Forge Canvas and Roadworks Circuit maps. [Build your own battleground](/blog/forge-building) is the full tour, and there is a [pack workshop](/forge) on the Hub.

New since that post: automatic doors now open in Slayer and every other mode, not just Forge. Forge also checks saved layouts and refuses malformed ones, with the reason. The launcher now keeps a map's packs in place, and installs any packs a saved layout needs before you launch.

Forge comes from the [MJOLNIRForge mod](/mods/mjolnir-forge) on the Hub, so install it there if FORGE isn't in your list of game types. Editing is host only for now.

Reference: [Forge controls](/docs/notes/forge), [your first Forge build](/docs/guides/forge-guide), and [create a community Forge pack](/docs/guides/forge-pack-authoring).

## Game types and the lobby

- **Team Slayer** is new: Red against Blue on every map with Slayer. Teammate kills cost a point.
- **CTF flags** now carry Halo CE's red cobra and blue eagle banners, and they keep their colours when dropped or carried.
- **Team armour** is cleaner: CTF and Team Slayer put everyone in Mk V Classic in their team colour. Slayer still keeps your own armour.
- **GAME TYPE** has its own screen with icons, descriptions and team formats.
- **The lobby** shows the map and game type as two tiles side by side, with changed settings listed below.

## Match chat, Discord and the post-game vote

Press **T** for all chat or **Y** for team chat. Type `/` to see the commands you can use, and Tab completes them. Hosts get `/kick`, `/ban` and `/unban`. Chat shows its rules the first time you open it. It is logged to your player account, and a public match's chat appears on its Hub page.

Discord now shows you playing MJOLNIR Core, with your map, game type and session time. Public games with room can offer **Join Game** on your Discord profile, which can even start the game if it's closed. You'll need the Discord desktop app with activity sharing on. Joining from a second Discord account hasn't been fully verified yet, so tell us how it goes.

![The post-game screen: final standings on the left, and four map tiles to vote on with a countdown on the right. The scores here were filled in for this picture.](/blog-images/weekly-update-1/post-game-vote.jpg)

The post-game vote is now a grid of tiles with each map's picture, game type and votes. It mixes game types, so you won't get four Slayers in a row, and it only offers maps everyone has or can download. The screen also no longer stutters.

The kill feed got a full rebuild too. Rows are animated, with avatars, the game's own weapon icons, and medals from Double Kill to Killionaire. The score is now two bars that fill toward the win.

## Fixes for playing together

Most of these came straight from our October 24 playtest. Thank you to everyone who played.

- CTF and Team Slayer no longer end the moment the map loads with three or more players.
- A player rejoining after a drop no longer takes the whole fireteam down with them.
- Players who join a match in progress now hear reloads, grenades, melee and equipment, including after leaving and rejoining.
- New players no longer inherit the score of whoever left their seat.
- Fixed crashes at the start of a second match and when quitting soon after a match.
- A killing spree arriving just after a Triple Kill no longer leaves a medal stuck on screen.
- The scoreboard marks who is dead until they respawn.
- Falling into Gephyrophobia's canyon kills you again.

**Still open:** joiners crashing on a map change. We removed one likely cause, but we aren't calling it fixed until a longer playtest confirms it. [Issue #262](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/issues/262) tracks it.

## Smoother, faster maps

The remastered maps got a lot of attention after launch.

- **A steady stutter is gone** from the remastered maps. Walking the same route on Death Island, long frames fell from 269 in 44 seconds to 28 in 52 seconds.
- **Loading hitches shrank.** Grass, rocks and trees are now built into the map instead of placed as it loads. On Death Island, the longest frame during loading fell from 15.5 seconds to under a second. The downloads are bigger as a result.
- **Grass stopped drawing across the whole map.** Some bands never culled at any distance. Wind is now off at Low and Medium foliage, so if a remastered map runs slowly, try lowering Foliage in Video settings.
- **Occasional script stutters are gone.** The worst frame in our Death Island test fell from 54 ms to 17 ms. That test was on one PC, standing still.
- **Rivers start full.** Battle Creek's and Timberland's rivers no longer take up to a minute to fill.
- **Bullets now stop on Death Island's swapped trees and rocks**, and grass grows right up to the rocks.

These figures come from our own test PC, so your results will vary. To help us see other hardware, type `/bench` in match chat. It takes about a minute and sends us the timings with your GPU and settings. If a map stutters for you, send us the `hitches.log` file from the MJOLNIRHud folder.

## A launcher that keeps you ready to play

Fireteam games need everyone on the same versions, so the launcher now handles that for you.

- **Launch checks first.** It looks at your mods, runtime and maps, and lists anything out of date or damaged. The file check takes under a second.
- **It updates itself first**, then offers Update and launch or Cancel. Being offline never blocks a launch.
- **The game tells you too.** The main menu shows what's out of date, with UPDATE AND RESTART or NOT NOW.
- **Other mods can step aside.** Mods MJOLNIR didn't install can break a game for the whole fireteam, so the launcher offers to move them aside while you play. They come back afterwards, and nothing is deleted.
- **Intro videos are skipped by default.** On our test PC, the main menu arrived in 28 seconds instead of 49. The switch is under Settings > Troubleshooting.
- **Crash reports are opt-in.** After a crash, the launcher asks whether to send a report. Nothing goes unless you click Send report, and What's sent? shows exactly what's included.

## The Hub

![The redesigned maps page on mjolnircore.com, with filters for game mode, game, size and vehicles.](/blog-images/weekly-update-1/hub-maps.jpg)

The [Hub](/maps) has a new look, with shared cards and filters across maps, mods, players and games. The maps page can now filter by Halo CE or Halo 2. [Match history](/matches) has moved to cards with map art, winners and the top three. It lists real matches by default, and an All matches toggle shows the rest. Match pages have a new header and a ranked scoreboard.

## For modders and map makers

- **Scripts in baked levels now load.** They were being dropped at load time. [CLI 0.7.0](/changelog/cli/0.7.0) fixes this and lets a level bring its own scripts. Published maps change only when they're baked again, so test with a joiner before you release.
- **Megalo game types:** `mjolnir megalo dump` reads any game type, and `megalo validate` checks that the game can load one safely ([CLI 0.5.0](/changelog/cli/0.5.0)).
- **Three cheats are back:** `cheat_all_weapons`, `cheat_all_vehicles` and `drop_safe` work with the [MJOLNIRBlamConsole mod](/mods/mjolnir-blam-console). They've been tested in solo campaign only.
- **The docs were audited** against the code on October 21, which fixed 76 broken links. See the updated guides for [tag editing](/docs/guides/tag-editing-guide), [your first mod](/docs/guides/making-your-first-mod), [texture swapping](/docs/guides/texture-swapping) and [custom levels](/docs/guides/level-authoring).

## Versions

| Product | Now at | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Launcher | [0.21.0](/changelog/launcher/0.21.0) | From 0.14.0 |
| Code mods | [0.43.1](/changelog/mods/0.43.1) | From 0.24.0 |
| CE runtime | 1.17.0 | The launcher installs it |
| CLI | [0.7.0](/changelog/cli/0.7.0) | Scoop and Homebrew are still on 0.6.0 |
| Tag editor | [0.25.0](/changelog/tag-editor/0.25.0) | From 0.24.0 |

Every release is listed in the [changelog](/changelog).

## Tell us what you find

Grab the [latest launcher](/download), play a few matches, and tell us what breaks in our [Discord](https://discord.gg/9gxYZsByW9). See you next week.

posts.title: Build your own battleground: modular Forge packs
posts.author: MJOLNIR Core
posts.summary: Build with MJOLNIR's modular Forge kits, Warthog roads, automatic doors, gravity lifts and green teleporters. Tour Crossline, plan a first courtyard, and learn how to contribute your own model pack.
posts.body:
A floor becomes a courtyard. Add a ramp and it becomes a raised base. Connect two bases with a bridge, put a road underneath, and suddenly there is a map worth arguing over.

That is what we want building in Forge to feel like. The latest MJOLNIR update brings modular construction packs together with better placement controls and pieces that do something: doors that open as you approach, lifts that carry you to another route, and the familiar green glow of a Halo CE teleporter.

Get the latest launcher and mods, then explore the [Forge packs](/forge) and [maps](/maps) on the Hub. The screenshots below come from the game; the labelled studio renders show the actual model geometry with Blender lighting.

## Start with pieces that fit

There are two families of building materials: **Foundry** for structures and **Roadworks** for vehicle routes. Foundry also has a separately namespaced **Wide** kit, so larger construction does not silently change an older map's pieces.

| Kit | Pieces | What it is for |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Foundry 0.2 | 24 | The original compact blocks, floors, cover, frames and light fixtures |
| Foundry Wide 0.2 | 38 | Larger floors, walls, ramps, junctions, windows, doors, lifts and teleporter housings on a 4 m module |
| Roadworks 0.2 | 10 | Long roads, curves and ramps with open or guarded edges |

The scale comes from driving and walking around the pieces. Earlier roads felt cramped beside a Warthog, so Roadworks now has **16 metres of clear road width**. Wide's new floor is **16 × 16 m**, its broad ramps are **8 m wide**, and its vehicle doorway has an **8 × 5.5 m clear opening**. Those dimensions belong to the models themselves: builders should not have to stretch every piece before it is useful.

![Foundry Wide's 38 actual pieces, with dimensions and matching families. Blender catalogue render; glass and energy materials here are previews.](/blog-images/forge-building/foundry-wide.webp)

[Open the full-size Foundry Wide catalogue](/blog-images/forge-building/foundry-wide.webp) to read every label and dimension.

The kit gives you several ways to solve the same problem. A shallow ramp makes a long approach; a steeper one fits a smaller corner. Full walls close the perimeter, glazed walls preserve a sightline, and T-junctions or crosses let a bridge become a network of routes. The original Foundry lights provide warm, red and blue landmarks.

## Place it, line it up, keep it there

The new controls make a suspended bridge practical to build. Pick up a piece with **V**, choose its physics with **F3**, and drop it where you want it:

- **Normal** uses the object's usual physics.
- **Fixed** holds the placed object in space.
- **Phased** holds it in space and permits overlapping geometry while building.

**F4** cycles a position grid from 0.25 to 4 metres. **F10** selects a rotation snap, and comma/period turn the piece. The HUD keeps the settings visible. **F5** saves the layout; **F6** loads it again, including the object's physics properties.

The grid aligns placement to world coordinates. It does not automatically join road endpoints or detect a nearby edge. For precise construction, use Phased mode, line up the origins, and check the result from Spartan height. Native holding and collision can still affect a final turn.

Our new [Forge building guide](/docs/guides/forge-guide) walks through the controls and a complete first build.

## Give the room another way through

The new utility pieces make a layout more than a collection of solids.

**Automatic doors** pair a frame with a moving panel. Fixed or Phased panels open on approach and close after the path clears. Their visible models and native collision move together. Saving an open door stores its closed starting position, so the next session does not begin with the panel's origin stranded above the frame. Leave clearance overhead and provide another route around a door while testing your map.

![In-game: Crossline's vehicle gate with its panel raised above the frame, and a Spartan in the clear opening for scale.](/blog-images/forge-building/door.webp)

**Gravity lifts** offer a compact upward route. The lift station has four shallow walk-up ramps, a central launch area and a nearby landing in Crossline. Walk in, rise, then steer toward the gallery. It is a useful alternative to putting another long ramp in every room.

![In-game: the lift's four ground approaches and the adjacent raised landing. The blue centre marks the launch area.](/blog-images/forge-building/lift.webp)

**Teleporters** have an animated green field based on the CE effect, while the native sender/receiver markers handle travel. The visible housing alone is not a destination: place the markers, give them a matching channel, and test both ends with room to step away from the trigger.

![In-game: Crossline's green teleporter field on a raised base. The two ends were tested for travel in both directions.](/blog-images/forge-building/portal.webp)

**Glass and windows** let players read the next space before entering it. These panes are transparent and solid, which makes them useful for observation corridors and separating routes without hiding them from one another.

![In-game: a cyan glass wall in the utility lane, with the glazed window and glass corner visible through it. Each pane blocks walking from either side.](/blog-images/forge-building/glass.webp)

## Three ways to put the kit to work

### A first courtyard

Start small: one 16 × 16 m floor, one broad ramp, six wall sections and two low cover pieces. That is ten pieces, with a finished deck 2 m above the ground. The ramp meets the floor, the walls give the space a boundary, and the opening is wide enough to understand at a glance.

![Build plan: ten pieces form a 16 × 16 m raised courtyard, with an 8 m-wide approach ramp. The guide gives the placement recipe.](/blog-images/forge-building/courtyard-plan.svg)

Build this first, walk every join, then add a window, another entrance or an upper route. The [step-by-step guide](/docs/guides/forge-guide#build-a-raised-courtyard) includes a parts list and planning coordinates. A blank **Forge Canvas** provides a 64 × 64 m starting deck; its palette must be baked with the Wide kit before using this particular recipe.

Once the joins work, the same idea grows into something like this:

![Blender assembly study: 31 unchanged Wide pieces form a 32 × 32 m courtyard with a raised gallery, ramp, bridge, door, lift and portal. This is a layout illustration, not an additional playable map; materials use Blender previews.](/blog-images/forge-building/assembly.webp)

### A red-versus-blue arena

**Crossline** is the larger playable showcase: **96 × 160 m**, with raised bases, broad approaches, side galleries and an open ground route for Warthogs. The utility lanes let you try the new pieces without making a door or lift the only way across the arena. Its 9 m perimeter keeps the construction enclosed.

![In-game aerial view of Crossline 0.3, built from the modular kits. The raised routes and the open lower arena occupy different heights.](/blog-images/forge-building/crossline-overview.webp)

![Crossline layout plan derived from its authored placements and routes. Colours distinguish the two bases and the utility areas.](/blog-images/forge-building/crossline-plan.svg)

All twenty new Wide pieces appear in the map, and all 38 are available in its Forge palette. The map includes team-owned base spawns and neutral midfield starts for free-for-all Slayer. That distinction matters: a map can look finished and still give a game type nowhere valid to spawn a player.

### A Warthog circuit

**Roadworks** uses straight sections, 45° and 90° curves, and ramps that rise 4 m over a 48 m run. The curves have a 40 m centreline radius. Guarded versions put barriers outside the clear road width; open versions are useful for intersections, pit entries and places where a builder wants a separate boundary.

![Roadworks' ten actual models, including long straights, curved connections and raised approaches. Blender catalogue render with all pieces shown at the same scale.](/blog-images/forge-building/roadworks.webp)

The **Roadworks Circuit** test map joins them into an approximately 731 m loop with a pit and raised route on a 320 × 320 m recovery deck. Use it as a starting point for driving experiments. The kit supplies the road geometry; race checkpoints and lap timing are separate future work.

## Bring your own pieces

We want community authors to expand the vocabulary: another architectural style, a set of columns and arches, industrial interiors, outdoor cover, or a racing kit with its own character.

You can contribute at two levels. **Model authors** can submit original source geometry, dimensions, collision shapes, previews and a small example layout in a pull request. **Pack authors** can take that work through the full build, test and signing process to produce a `.mjolnir` content archive. A `.blend` file is an authoring source, not something the game can place directly.

The [community pack-authoring guide](/docs/guides/forge-pack-authoring) covers the process:

1. **Design a small, consistent set.** Use real dimensions, stable origins and deliberate join heights. For a kit that fits Wide, start from its 4 m module and test against a Spartan and a Warthog early.
2. **Build both appearance and collision.** A convincing visual mesh needs matching collision and physics. Keep glass solid where intended and keep decorative energy out of the passage.
3. **Give the pack its own identity.** A catalogue supplies names, categories, dimensions and namespaced piece IDs. Optional lights, lifts and doors use bounded data fields rather than scripts supplied by the pack.
4. **Test a small map.** Place, rotate, freeze, save and reload the pieces. Walk the seams, drive the corners, and check that a doorway is actually clear.
5. **Package, sign and submit the release.** The guide includes the build commands and explains the Hub's author-key, upload and validation requirements. Your catalogue gives other builders a way to discover the pieces and see what fits their map.

A map declares its pack dependencies and supported palette when it is baked. The launcher resolves the required releases before play, downloading missing dependencies, and saved Forge layouts record the pack releases they were built with. A pack can be updated later, but an update has to keep every piece that existing maps and layouts use, and the Hub checks that before it publishes one. Downloading another pack does not add arbitrary new entries to an already-baked map's palette. Those boundaries keep a later asset update from quietly changing someone else's level.

## Make a place of your own

Start with a route you want to play: a courtyard with two entrances, a bridge worth fighting over, or a curve you can take at speed. Build its outline, walk or drive it, and add detail once the space feels right.

[Follow the building guide](/docs/guides/forge-guide), [create a pack](/docs/guides/forge-pack-authoring), or browse the [source kits](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/tree/main/forge-packs). A useful first contribution can be one good wall, one reliable ramp, and a place that shows why they belong together.

posts.title: Ten Halo CE maps, remastered in Campaign Evolved's look
posts.author: MJOLNIR Core
posts.summary: Nine classic maps and Yoyorast Island now look like they belong in Campaign Evolved: real terrain and grass, the game's own rock and trees, a living ocean and rivers, and Halo CE's lamps lit by Unreal. Drag the pictures to compare, then see how it was built and where the code lives.
posts.body:
![Death Island's beach, remastered](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/death-island-beach.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/death-island-beach-classic.jpg)

The classic maps came to Halo Campaign Evolved looking like Halo CE, and
[lighting them with Unreal Engine](/blog/lighting-the-classics) kept them that
way: the same surfaces, the same colours, real light. This update goes
further on nine of them and on Yoyorast Island. Their ground, rock, grass, trees and water are now
drawn the way Campaign Evolved draws its own levels. The layout and every
weapon, vehicle and flag spawn stay exactly where Halo CE put them. The new
rocks and tree trunks are solid where they stand, as Halo CE's boulders and
trees were.

The ten are Blood Gulch, Death Island, Ice Fields, Sidewinder, Timberland,
Infinity, Gephyrophobia, Battle Creek and Rat Race, plus the Custom Edition
community's Yoyorast Island.

**Update, October 18:** Danger Canyon has joined them, as
version 2.0.0 with CE runtime pack 1.10.0.

Every comparison below is the current hub version of a map (left) against
the remastered one (right), from the same camera. Drag the divider to compare.

## What changed

- **Real terrain.** The ground under each outdoor map is rebuilt as an
  Unreal Engine landscape from Halo CE's own heights. Sand turns to earth
  and gravel inland, banks go green as they steepen, and the beaches get
  ripples you can see from eye level.
- **Grass that grows.** Several kinds of grass, weeds and tufts, at
  different heights, on the ground Halo CE painted green, moving in the
  wind. Pebbles and driftwood scatter where it painted sand. Nothing grows
  under a roof, where it would only stand in the dark.
- **Campaign Evolved's rock and trees.** Cliffs are drawn in the game's own
  layered rock with real depth, instead of one tiled texture, and the
  campaign's cliff stones are set into the walls. Halo CE's boulders and
  trees become the campaign's own, sized to match.
- **Water that moves.** Death Island and Yoyorast sit in a real ocean that
  swells and breaks on the sand, over a sea floor that falls away from the
  shore. Timberland's and Battle Creek's streams are now rivers that run
  along their beds and over their falls.
- **Tracks in the sand.** Drive a Warthog across a beach and it leaves tyre
  tracks, as the campaign's own beaches do. Footprints follow you too.
- **Halo CE's lamps, lit by Unreal.** The light fixtures Halo CE placed now
  cast real light and shadow.
- **Snow.** Ice Fields, Sidewinder and Gephyrophobia get snow-covered ground
  and rock, and Ice Fields and Sidewinder get falling snow.
- **Metal.** The metal the bases share has the game's Forerunner finish:
  fine scratches and wear that catch the light, without changing Halo CE's
  colours.
- **Life.** Birds over the cliffs, gulls along the shore, falling leaves and
  wind.

## Blood Gulch

The canyon walls are the campaign's desert rock, the paths are packed earth,
and grass covers the valley floor. Halo CE's boulders and trees are the
campaign's own.

![Blood Gulch from the cliff top](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/blood-gulch-overview.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/blood-gulch-overview-classic.jpg)

![Blood Gulch's red base](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/blood-gulch-base.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/blood-gulch-base-classic.jpg)

![The valley path](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/blood-gulch-valley.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/blood-gulch-valley-classic.jpg)

![A boulder by the blue base](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/blood-gulch-boulder.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/blood-gulch-boulder-classic.jpg)

## Death Island

Sand beaches with ripples and pebbles, a real ocean with surf, grass on the
banks and layered cliffs. The island's trees have full canopies, and its
twenty light fixtures light the bases.

![Death Island from above the bay](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/death-island-overview.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/death-island-overview-classic.jpg)

![The beach at eye level](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/death-island-low-beach.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/death-island-low-beach-classic.jpg)

![The shore](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/death-island-shore.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/death-island-shore-classic.jpg)

![A cliff over the beach](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/death-island-cliff.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/death-island-cliff-classic.jpg)

## Yoyorast Island

The Custom Edition community map gets the same ocean as Death Island. The
sea floor rises into shallows around the pillars standing in the water, so
the waves feel them and break around them. Sand rings its islets and grass
climbs its terraces.

![Yoyorast from the bay](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/yoyorast-overlook.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/yoyorast-overlook-classic.jpg)

![The islet's beach, across the channel](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/yoyorast-beach.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/yoyorast-beach-classic.jpg)

![Grass against the cliff](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/yoyorast-grass.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/yoyorast-grass-classic.jpg)

![The islet](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/yoyorast-island.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/yoyorast-island-classic.jpg)

## Ice Fields

Snow on the ground and on the rock, glacial stone in the walls and snow
falling across the bridge.

![The bridge](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/ice-fields-bridge.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/ice-fields-bridge-classic.jpg)

![The tunnel gate](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/ice-fields-gate.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/ice-fields-gate-classic.jpg)

![The snow field below](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/ice-fields-snowfield.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/ice-fields-snowfield-classic.jpg)

## Sidewinder

The frozen canyon under the ring: snow-covered ground, frozen pools, and
rock and trees in the campaign's winter look.

![Under the ring](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/sidewinder-ring.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/sidewinder-ring-classic.jpg)

![By the glacier wall](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/sidewinder-glacier.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/sidewinder-glacier-classic.jpg)

![The rock ridge](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/sidewinder-ridge.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/sidewinder-ridge-classic.jpg)

## Timberland

A forest floor of grass and weeds, and a river that finally runs: from the
falls down the whole valley.

![The river](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/timberland-river.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/timberland-river-classic.jpg)

![The valley](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/timberland-valley.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/timberland-valley-classic.jpg)

![Through the trees](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/timberland-forest.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/timberland-forest-classic.jpg)

![A lone pine](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/timberland-tree.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/timberland-tree-classic.jpg)

## Infinity

The huge open map gets real terrain and grass from end to end, and land and
haze out to the horizon. In Halo CE, Infinity's rim ended in a black band
under the sky.

![Out to the horizon, from above the blue base](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/infinity-horizon.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/infinity-horizon-classic.jpg)

![A canyon path under the bridges](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/infinity-path.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/infinity-path-classic.jpg)

![Grass along the canyon floor](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/infinity-canyon.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/infinity-canyon-classic.jpg)

## Gephyrophobia

The canyon is the campaign's glacial rock under snow. Halo CE drew the fog
in the chasm below the bridge as a flat sheet, so the rock stopped dead at a
hard line. Now it is real height fog, and the walls fade into it.

![The bridge](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/gephyrophobia-bridge.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/gephyrophobia-bridge-classic.jpg)

![The cliff fading into the chasm's fog](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/gephyrophobia-chasm.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/gephyrophobia-chasm-classic.jpg)

![The red end of the bridge](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/gephyrophobia-pylon.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/gephyrophobia-pylon-classic.jpg)

## Battle Creek

The creek is real water now. It runs the length of the canyon in its bed,
under the overhangs and into the pools at either end. The walls are the
campaign's rock and the banks are grass.

![The creek at water level](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/battle-creek-stream.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/battle-creek-stream-classic.jpg)

![The creek under the overhangs](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/battle-creek-creek.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/battle-creek-creek-classic.jpg)

## Danger Canyon

Added on October 18. The canyon floor is real terrain under grass and
weeds, the walls are the campaign's rock, and Halo CE's granite boulders
and pines are now the game's own. The bridge structure and the bases are
untouched.

![The bridge, from the canyon rim](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/danger-canyon-front.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/danger-canyon-front-classic.jpg)

![The canyon floor](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/danger-canyon-floor.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/danger-canyon-floor-classic.jpg)

![Behind the blue base](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/danger-canyon-base.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/danger-canyon-base-classic.jpg)

![A boulder under the bridge](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/danger-canyon-bridge.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/danger-canyon-bridge-classic.jpg)

## Rat Race

Rat Race has no outdoor ground, so it gets no landscape or grass. Its
tunnels are cut through the same rock as Battle Creek's cliffs, and that
rock is now the game's own, with real depth, lit by Halo CE's own light as
the original was.

![A tunnel through the rock](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/rat-race-tunnel.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/rat-race-tunnel-classic.jpg)

![The cave room beside it](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/rat-race-room.jpg?before=/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/rat-race-room-classic.jpg)

## How it was made

None of this is placed by hand. Each map goes through one pipeline, from the
converted Halo CE map to a finished map pack, and running it again after a
change rebuilds the map exactly. A map's entry in one config file says
which of its shaders are ground and which are cliffs, where its rivers run
and what its sea does. Everything below is driven from there.

### From triangles to a heightmap

Halo CE has no terrain system. Blood Gulch's ground is a few thousand
triangles in the same mesh as its bases and cliffs, painted with blended
textures and Bungie's baked light. Campaign Evolved's beaches are Unreal
Engine landscapes: a grid of heights that gets grass, footprints, tyre
tracks and the game's own ground materials.

So the first step samples Halo CE's ground onto a regular grid, one height
every metre over Blood Gulch, and writes it out as a 16-bit heightmap.
Where two layers of ground overlap, such as a plateau whose lip overhangs
the cliff below, the grid takes the lower one. Wherever the grid can't
follow the shape (cliffs, overhangs, bases, steps of more than two metres
between neighbouring samples), the landscape is cut away and Halo CE's own
mesh draws that spot instead. In the picture below the dark areas are cut
away, and you can still see Bungie's triangles in the shading.

![Blood Gulch's heightmap](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/blood-gulch-heightmap.jpg)

The landscape's material is Campaign Evolved's own: Megascans sand, earth,
gravel and grass, blended by what Halo CE painted at each point and by the
slope. It also reads a top-down bake of Halo CE's light, so the shadows of
the cliffs and bases fall exactly where they did in 2001.

### Procedural grass, pebbles and wall rock

The grass, weeds, pebbles, driftwood and the rocks set into the cliffs are
placed by a procedural generator we wrote for this, which runs when the map
is built. Its rules come from Campaign Evolved itself: we read the B30
beach's placements straight out of the game's World Partition cells and
copied its densities, sizes and heights above the sea.

For each rule, the generator:

1. **Asks Halo CE what the ground is.** Halo CE's ground shaders blend two
   detail textures, such as sand and grass, by the base texture's alpha.
   The generator works that blend out at every point, so it knows how much
   grass and how much sand is there. Grass grows where Halo CE drew grass,
   pebbles lie where it drew sand, and tufts line the edge between them.
2. **Clusters it.** A smooth noise field decides where clumps gather and
   where the ground stays bare, so the grass grows in patches rather than as
   an even carpet.
3. **Throws out what doesn't fit.** Points on slopes too steep for the rule
   are dropped, and so are points under a roof, so nothing grows in a
   tunnel. Nothing tall goes where players walk. Halo CE's simulation knows
   only Halo CE's collision, so a knee-high rock would be something to walk
   through.
4. **Seeds everything.** Every point is random but seeded, so every PC
   places the same blade of grass in the same spot. Your opponent sees the
   tuft you are hiding behind.

The rocks in the cliffs work the other way round. The generator walks the
cliff faces, picks spots where a rock would sit against the wall, and lights
each rock with the Halo CE light on the wall behind it, so a rock in shade
stays in shade.

The result is one file of instances that the level loader spawns as
instanced meshes when the map loads: almost 300,000 on Blood Gulch alone.

![Blood Gulch's procedural scatter](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/blood-gulch-scatter.jpg)

Halo CE's own boulders and trees are swapped rather than scattered. Each
tree is rebuilt from a real tree in B30's cells, with its trunk and canopy
pieces kept in the same arrangement, and each boulder is sized to the
Halo CE model it replaces. Their collision is merged into the map's own, so
they are solid in game.

### Rock with real depth

The cliffs use a material of our own built on the game's rock. It projects
the campaign's jagged Megascans rock from three directions, so it never
stretches the way Halo CE's 1024 x 256 cliff strip did over a twenty-metre
wall. Halo CE's own colours come through as banding, and its baked light
works as occlusion, so the clefts stay dark.

The cliff walls are then rebuilt as a Nanite mesh and tessellated, so the
rock's height map pushes the surface in and out for real. Halo CE's map
geometry splits every vertex where two faces meet, and moving those apart
would open a crack along every edge, so all the vertices at one point are
welded to a single normal first. The displacement fades out toward the
edges where a wall meets the ground. Rat Race's tunnels are lit by Halo CE's
lightmap instead, since no sun reaches them.

### Simulated water

The ocean and rivers are Fluid Flux, the shallow-water simulation Campaign
Evolved uses for its own rivers and beaches, running live in the map.

- **The ocean.** The landscape's floor shelves away from the shore under the
  sea, so the waves have something to break on, and an apron of shallows
  around the structures standing in the water lets the waves feel them.
  Splashes run along the waterline. A mask keeps the sea and its fog out of
  the tunnels that dip below sea level.
- **Rivers.** The simulation sees the ground from above, so under an
  overhang it would take the rock's top for the river bed. Each river gets a
  bed of its own that only the simulation sees: the lowest surface at every
  point inside the river's banks, and walls it can't climb outside them.

Death Island's heightmap shows the new sea floor: the blue around the island
is ground Halo CE never had, shelving down from the beach so the surf has
somewhere to break.

![Death Island's heightmap, with its new sea floor](/blog-images/ce-maps-remastered/death-island-heightmap.jpg)

### Halo CE's lamps, in Unreal

Halo CE placed its light fixtures in the map data. Each one becomes an
Unreal point light in the same place, with the same colour and strength,
stepped a little out of its fixture so the fixture doesn't shade its own
lamp. Halo CE's walls are one-sided, and the sun leaked through every inside
corner. So a copy of every wall, set slightly behind it, casts the shadows.

## Help make it better

All of this is open source, and every piece is a file you can read and
change. If you want to help, start here:

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| The pipeline: one command per map | [`tools/level/upgrade_ce_map.py`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/tools/level/upgrade_ce_map.py) |
| Each map's settings | [`tools/level/ce_upgrade_maps.json`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/tools/level/ce_upgrade_maps.json) |
| Heightmaps, holes and bakes | [`tools/level/build_landscape.py`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/tools/level/build_landscape.py) |
| Procedural grass, pebbles and wall rock | [`tools/level/scatter_foliage.py`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/tools/level/scatter_foliage.py) |
| Trees and boulders swapped for the campaign's | [`tools/level/scenery_swap.py`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/tools/level/scenery_swap.py) |
| Their collision | [`tools/level/b30_collision.py`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/tools/level/b30_collision.py) |
| Tessellated cliffs | [`tools/level/cliff_mesh.py`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/tools/level/cliff_mesh.py) |
| The sea floor and the wading line | [`tools/level/sea_zone.py`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/tools/level/sea_zone.py) |
| The materials: ground, rock, metal | [`unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_ce_materials.py`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_ce_materials.py) |
| The landscape world | [`unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_ce_landscape.py`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_ce_landscape.py) |
| Everything at runtime: grass, rock, water, footprints, lights | [`mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/main.lua`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/main.lua) |
| The map packs | [`tools/level/pack_remastered.py`](https://github.com/devnull9090/mjolnir-core/blob/main/tools/level/pack_remastered.py) |

Each script opens with a description of what it does, and most decisions in
the code carry a comment saying what went wrong without them. Some good
first projects: another map through the pipeline, new scatter rules for a biome, or better
placement for the rocks on steep walls. Open an issue or a pull request on
GitHub, or find us on Discord.

## Getting it

The remastered maps arrive as an ordinary update to each map. Update the
launcher first, then update the ten maps in it. The remastered maps carry
their grass and decal files beside the level, and they need CE runtime pack
1.8.0, which the updated launcher installs for you. Maps downloaded in game
update the same way.

Danger Canyon needs CE runtime pack 1.10.0, which the launcher installs the
same way.

The other nine classic maps are unchanged. They are mostly indoor or built
maps, with little ground or rock to remaster.

posts.title: Lighting the classics: teaching Unreal Engine to light Halo CE's maps
posts.author: MJOLNIR Core
posts.summary: The nineteen classic maps are lit by Unreal Engine while still looking like Halo CE. Their lightmaps are baked by our own solver at up to eight times Halo CE's resolution, and since 1.4.0 they have Halo CE's fog, MCC's teleporter and light shaders, and the right brightness. Here is how we got there.
posts.body:
![Blood Gulch, lit by Unreal Engine with Halo CE's colours](/blog-images/lighting-the-classics/blood-gulch.jpg)

*Updated 2026-10-09 for classic maps 1.4.0, CE runtime 1.5.0 and mods
0.19.0: fog, MCC's transparent shaders, a sky that sits where Halo CE puts
it, and maps that are no longer drawn too bright. Every screenshot and every
comparison with the alpha is retaken on the 1.4.0 maps. The 1.4.0 changes
come first below, then the 1.3.0 solver, then the 1.2.0 story they build
on.*

When the classic maps came to Halo Campaign Evolved
[in the alpha](/blog/classic-multiplayer-alpha), they looked like Halo CE
because, in a sense, they *were* Halo CE: every surface carried the light
Bungie baked into it in 2001, painted on like a photograph. That made them
faithful, and it also made them deaf. Campaign Evolved runs on Unreal Engine 5,
which has real lights and real shadows, and none of it could reach the
ground. Switch on a Warthog's headlights and the road stayed dark, while every
player and vehicle in the beam turned glowing white.

The 1.2.0 maps changed that: they keep Halo CE's colours and its soft shade,
but the light on them comes from Unreal Engine. The 1.3.0 maps went one step
further and replaced Bungie's lightmaps with ones we bake ourselves, and the
1.4.0 maps add the fog and the effect shaders the PC version never had.
Here's the difference between the alpha and now, from the same spots:

![Timberland, alpha and now](/blog-images/lighting-the-classics/timberland-alpha-vs-now.jpg)

![Battle Creek, alpha and now](/blog-images/lighting-the-classics/battle-creek-alpha-vs-now.jpg)

![Death Island, alpha and now](/blog-images/lighting-the-classics/death-island-alpha-vs-now.jpg)

## 1.4.0: fog, MCC's shaders and the right brightness

### Everything was 1.7 times too bright

Death Island's bases came out white, while MCC draws them grey. The cause
went back to before the classic maps had worlds of their own. Back then they
loaded into a campaign level's world, and that world applies a colour
correction that darkens every frame to 0.6 of its value. Our materials
divided by 0.6 to undo it. Since September each map loads into its own
world, which applies no such correction, but the division stayed. So every
Halo CE surface on every map was drawn 1/0.6, or about 1.7, times too bright.
The materials no longer divide, and a lightmap texel of 0.91 now shows as
0.91.

![A Death Island base wall, 1.3.0 and 1.4.0](/blog-images/lighting-the-classics/death-island-base-wall.jpg)

The difference holds outdoors too. The maps keep their colour and their
shade, but they are no longer washed out:

![Death Island, 1.3.0 and 1.4.0](/blog-images/lighting-the-classics/death-island-1.4.0.jpg)

### Fog

Five of the classic maps have a fog plane: Damnation's shaft,
Gephyrophobia's chasm, and the water on Battle Creek, Chill Out and Death
Island. Anything under the plane fades into the fog's colour, more the
deeper it is and the further away. Our converter never carried those planes
over, so Gephyrophobia's chasm was a black pit, and you couldn't tell how far
down it went.

The converter now reads each plane and its fog from the map, and the
materials draw it the way MCC's environment shaders do. They follow the same
recipe: how deep under the plane a surface is and how far it is from the eye,
each against the fog's opaque depth and distance, mixed by how deep the eye
itself is.

![Gephyrophobia's chasm, 1.3.0 and 1.4.0](/blog-images/lighting-the-classics/gephyrophobia-fog.jpg)

![Chill Out's pool, 1.3.0 and 1.4.0](/blog-images/lighting-the-classics/chill-out-fog.jpg)

One attempt cut the fog off at the outline of its plane. That drew a
hard-edged slab across Chill Out's lower floor, while MCC fogs the whole
floor, because Halo CE fogs every part of the level the fog's region touches.
The maps now fog everything under the plane's height, which matches MCC on
all five.

### MCC's teleporters and light volumes

Halo CE on the Xbox had a flexible shader for effects like teleporter fields,
power-ups and beams of light. The 2003 PC version drew all of them with a
simpler stand-in, and those stand-ins are all a classic map file carries.
Rat Race's teleporter was a soft green blob tiled from two dust textures.
MCC's Halo CE editing kit ships the original shaders at the same paths, so the
converter now draws those instead, with a port of MCC's own shader code.

![Rat Race's teleporter, 1.3.0 and 1.4.0](/blog-images/lighting-the-classics/rat-race-teleporter.jpg)

Fifteen shaders now draw MCC's originals, among them the teleporter fields,
beacons and Damnation's light volumes. A few change with the live object,
like Gephyrophobia's field generator shield, and those keep the PC version:
without the object's state they drew white or red where MCC draws purple.

![Damnation, 1.3.0 and 1.4.0](/blog-images/lighting-the-classics/damnation-shaft.jpg)

Damnation's light volumes also used to strobe. They flicker on purpose, but
we picked a new random brightness thirty times per flicker, which at their
0.6-second period meant 50 changes a second. They now drift smoothly.

### The sky, and cliffs in the dark

Halo CE draws the sky around the camera, wherever it is. Ours was a fixed
mesh centred on the middle of the level's bounding box. On Gephyrophobia that
put it 525 metres under the bridge, so the Halo ring rose from the wrong
place. The sky now moves with the camera. The ring also tore where two of its
strips met. Every texture we copied from MCC's tags, and every reflection
cube map, was being read three texels out of place, because the file writer
added 12 bytes of padding after the header.

Last, a fix for headlights. On the solver-lit maps, a face turned away from
the sun got no Unreal-lit colour at all, so headlights, muzzle flashes and
explosions stopped at a hard line where a cliff turned from the sun. Both
sides now get a share of it. Sunlit faces are unchanged, and Unreal's sun
still adds nothing to the far side.

## Baking the light ourselves

Halo CE's lightmaps were computed once, in 2001, by a tool in Bungie's
editing kit, and stored in the map files at the resolution a 2001 PC could
afford: a whole base shares a 256-pixel page, so one texel of light covers a
metre of wall. Everything we did in 1.2.0 had to work from those pages. Unreal
drew its own sharp sun shadow on the ground, but the lightmap underneath still
carried Halo CE's blurry copy of the same shadow, and on a Blood Gulch base
